The rest of the deck ('A Short and Decisive Mill—Sporting News and Notes—Ball Gossip') refers to separate items below in the column, which are not about Allen.

title.suggested: Daly-McManus fight called off; Allen said to have put up the whole $1,000 stake

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that the Daly-McManus fight was off and the stakes would be returned, and repeated talk that Tom Allen had put up all of McManus's $1,000 and stuck on technicalities rather than lose it.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Monday, December 10, 1888', page 8. The current title is misleading: the stakes were to be returned to both sides, so Allen did not lose the $1,000.

facts.fact: Allen backed McManus, 'the stranger from Kansas City', against Dan Daly; a well-known sporting man said Allen put up the first $250 forfeit and, when other backers failed to come forward, every later deposit until the whole $1,000 was his

The Daly-McManus fight was called off, with stakeholder Bill Clark to return the money to both sides; Daly said McManus had got Allen mixed up in it and both wanted out, and it was said Allen stuck on technicalities rather than fight or forfeit

notes: McManus's first name is not given; facts-index has 'Spars with Hugh McManus in 1888', possibly the same man. Allen is called 'the fat and festive Thomas'.
